title: Investment Management and Private Markets Supervision
summary: A ten-module programme equipping supervisors to oversee investment, wealth and private market managers, including private credit, leverage, valuation and non-bank systemic risk.
intro: This training programme equips supervisory staff to oversee investment managers, wealth managers and private markets: assessing governance, mandates and client outcomes, challenging valuation, leverage and liquidity mismatch, and responding to systemic and retail risks in non-bank finance.

sections.Aim and Purpose: To give supervisors an informed view of the investment management business itself, from discretionary and wealth management to private equity and private credit, and of the risks it now poses to clients and to financial stability. Participants leave able to test managers' governance, conflicts and portfolio practice, scrutinise private market valuation and leverage, and contribute to the authority's response to non-bank systemic risk and the retailisation of private markets.
sections.What It Covers: The investment management sector and non-bank financial intermediation, manager governance and substance, portfolio management and mandate compliance, wealth and discretionary management, remuneration, conflicts and performance disclosure, private equity and private credit, private market valuation, leverage and liquidity mismatch, non-bank systemic risk, and retail access to private markets.
Intended Audience: Supervisors and inspectors responsible for asset managers, wealth managers, discretionary managers and private fund managers
Financial stability, policy and risk specialists working on non-bank financial intermediation and private credit
Team leaders and heads of department setting priorities for asset and wealth management supervision
Learning Objectives: Explain how investment, wealth and private market managers operate and earn revenue
Assess manager governance, substance, remuneration and conflicts of interest
Evaluate portfolio management practice, mandate compliance and client outcomes in discretionary services
Challenge private market managers on valuation, leverage, liquidity and fees
Analyse non-bank systemic risk using FSB and IOSCO work and supervisory data
Design a supervisory response to the retailisation of private markets
sections.Structure and Format: Ten modules of about three hours each, delivered in person, virtually or in a hybrid format, either as a multi-day programme or as a series of half-day workshops. Each module combines a technical briefing with case studies, data exercises and supervisory question sets, and modules can be selected or tailored to the authority's asset and wealth management sector.
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience of supervising asset managers, funds or investment firms is helpful. No specialist private markets or quantitative background is required.
Core Reading: IOSCO, Thematic Analysis: Emerging Risks in Private Finance (2023)
FSB, Global Monitoring Report on Non-Bank Financial Intermediation (annual)
FSB, Revised Policy Recommendations to Address Structural Vulnerabilities from Liquidity Mismatch in Open-Ended Funds (2023)

modules.title: The Investment Management Sector and Non-Bank Finance
modules.summary: How asset, wealth and private market managers fit into the financial system, how their business models have changed, and why non-bank financial intermediation is now a supervisory priority.
objectives: Explain the business models and revenue drivers of investment managers
Distinguish the regulation of managers, products and client services
Describe the growth of non-bank financial intermediation and private markets
syllabus: Traditional, alternative, wealth and private market managers
Fee pressure, consolidation and the shift to passive and private assets
Manager, product and service regulation: where the perimeter sits
FSB and IOSCO work on non-bank financial intermediation

modules.title: Manager Governance, Substance and Delegation
modules.summary: How supervisors assess whether a manager is properly governed and genuinely in control of the activities it delegates, including in cross-border and platform structures.
objectives: Evaluate board composition, independence and oversight of investment risk
Assess substance, delegation and cross-border management structures
Identify letter-box and white-label red flags
syllabus: Governance, fit and proper requirements and key function holders
Delegation of portfolio and risk management and retained oversight
Cross-border management structures and substance tests
Host platforms and white-label managers: supervisory concerns

modules.title: Portfolio Management Practice and Mandate Compliance
modules.summary: How portfolio managers construct and manage portfolios against mandates and risk budgets, and how supervisors test the independence and effectiveness of investment risk oversight.
objectives: Explain mandate-driven portfolio construction and risk budgeting
Assess pre-trade and post-trade mandate compliance controls
Evaluate the independence of investment risk management
syllabus: Investment process, mandates and risk budgets
Mandate breaches, investment restrictions and compliance monitoring
Trade allocation, cross trades and dealing errors
Exercise: testing mandate compliance on a sample portfolio

modules.title: Wealth and Discretionary Management: Client Outcomes
modules.summary: How wealth and discretionary managers serve private clients through model portfolios, platforms and bespoke mandates, and how supervisors test suitability, costs and value.
objectives: Assess suitability in discretionary and model portfolio services
Evaluate costs, charges and value across the distribution chain
Identify poor outcomes from ongoing advice and portfolio drift
syllabus: Discretionary, advisory and model portfolio services
Ongoing suitability reviews and portfolio drift
Layered costs: platforms, managers, funds and advice
Vulnerable and high-net-worth clients: distinct supervisory risks

modules.title: Remuneration, Conflicts of Interest and Performance Disclosure
modules.summary: How manager remuneration and ownership create incentives, how conflicts of interest arise across clients and products, and how supervisors test performance claims used in marketing.
objectives: Assess whether remuneration structures create inappropriate incentives
Identify and evaluate conflicts of interest across clients and products
Challenge performance measurement, attribution and marketing claims
syllabus: Remuneration policies, deferral and performance fees
Conflicts registers, allocation fairness and in-house product bias
Performance measurement, composites and industry presentation standards
Misleading performance claims and backtested results

modules.title: Private Equity and Private Credit: Structures and Risks
modules.summary: How private equity and private credit funds raise, deploy and return capital, the financing techniques now common in private markets, and the risks these create for investors and the system.
objectives: Explain private equity and private credit fund structures and lifecycles
Assess fund finance, continuation vehicles and other liquidity techniques
Identify concentration and interconnectedness risks in private credit
syllabus: Buyout, growth, direct lending and asset-based finance strategies
Subscription lines, net asset value loans and payment-in-kind interest
Continuation vehicles and manager-led secondaries
Links between private credit, banks and insurers

modules.title: Valuation, Fees and Conflicts in Private Markets
modules.summary: Why valuation of private assets relies heavily on judgement, how fees and conflicts can distort valuations and investor outcomes, and how supervisors challenge valuation governance.
objectives: Explain valuation methods for private equity and private credit assets
Assess valuation governance, independence and use of third-party valuers
Identify red flags such as stale marks and valuation smoothing
syllabus: Valuation methods and the treatment of stressed and amended loans
Valuation committees, independent valuers and audit
Fees, expenses and conflicts in transactions between funds
Case study: challenging a private credit portfolio valuation

modules.title: Leverage, Liquidity Mismatch and Interconnectedness
modules.summary: How leverage builds up at fund, portfolio company and manager level, where liquidity mismatches arise in investment vehicles, and how stress transmits through margin calls and funding links.
objectives: Assess leverage across funds, portfolio companies and financing chains
Evaluate liquidity mismatch in open-ended and semi-liquid vehicles
Explain how margin calls and funding links transmit stress
syllabus: Financial and synthetic leverage and their measurement
Liquidity mismatch, redemption terms and liquidity management tools
Margin calls, collateral and procyclicality
Lessons from recent stress episodes in non-bank finance

modules.title: Non-Bank Systemic Risk and Supervisory Data
modules.summary: How authorities identify and monitor systemic risk outside the banking sector, close data gaps, and use macroprudential and supervisory tools in line with FSB and IOSCO recommendations.
objectives: Explain FSB and IOSCO recommendations on non-bank leverage and liquidity
Use supervisory data to monitor concentration, leverage and liquidity risk
Evaluate macroprudential and supervisory tools for non-bank risk
syllabus: Systemic risk channels: leverage, liquidity, interconnectedness and concentration
Data gaps and use of fund, manager and transaction reporting
Stress testing and system-wide exercises for non-bank finance
Macroprudential tools and cross-authority coordination

modules.title: Retailisation of Private Markets and Supervisory Response
modules.summary: Brings the programme together by examining how private market products are reaching retail and wealth investors, the investor protection risks this creates, and the authority's supervisory response.
objectives: Assess semi-liquid and long-term vehicles offered to retail investors
Evaluate distribution, suitability and disclosure for private market products
Produce a supervisory plan for managers and private markets
syllabus: Evergreen and semi-liquid funds, feeder structures and tokenised access
Distribution through wealth managers, platforms and retirement savings
Disclosure of fees, liquidity limits and valuation uncertainty
Workshop: a supervisory plan for private markets retailisation

related.title: Asset Management and Investment Fund Regulation: International Edition
related.summary: A ten-module programme mapping asset management and fund regulation through IOSCO and FSB standards, from fund regimes and delegation to liquidity, cross-border distribution, sustainability and resilience.

related.title: EU Asset Management and Investment Fund Regulation (EU Edition)
related.summary: A ten-module programme mapping EU fund and asset management regulation, from UCITS, AIFMD and MiFID II to liquidity, delegation, cross-border marketing, SFDR and DORA.

related.title: Fund Regulation Country Briefings
related.summary: Eleven country webinar briefings on fund vehicles, regulators, authorisation, distribution and recent developments in leading European, offshore and Asia Pacific fund markets.

related.title: International Fund Regulation: Global and Regional Briefings
related.summary: A ten-module webinar series mapping international, EU and Asia Pacific fund regulation and how cross-border fund distribution, management and investment are regulated.

related.title: Introduction to Investment Funds: From Launch to Wind-Down
related.summary: A fourteen-module foundation programme taking new funds professionals and supervisors through every stage of an investment fund, from structure and regulation to operations and wind-down.

related.title: Investment Funds Supervision
related.summary: A ten-module programme equipping supervisors to oversee investment funds and their managers, from authorisation and valuation to liquidity, leverage, private markets and tokenised funds.
